question.text: Why do Cat I/II AIFs organised as trusts prefer the 'irrevocable, determinate' trust form?

answer.text: Because SEBI mandates only determinate trusts for AIF registration under Regulation 4.
Because indeterminate trusts are only available to Cat III AIFs.
Because determinate trusts are exempt from the minimum 3-year close-ended requirement.
Because a determinate trust ensures each beneficiary's share is clearly ascertainable, which preserves Section 115UB pass-through taxation.

explanation.text: The Logic: Tax law requires each beneficiary's share to be determinable to grant pass-through (Section 115UB). In an 'irrevocable determinate' trust, each investor's beneficial interest is identified through unit allotment in the trust deed. An indeterminate trust may suffer MMR taxation at the fund level - defeating tax neutrality. The Trap: SEBI does not itself mandate determinacy; tax law does. Cat III exclusivity is fabricated. 3-year rule is independent. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C and the Taxation topic (Ch 13) reinforce 115UB. The determinacy requirement flows from Income-tax Act provisions, not SEBI Regulations. Manager's Pro-Tip: Tag every LP with a unit number in the trust deed register. Ambiguity on beneficial interest can flip the AIF into 'indeterminate' status and collapse pass-through treatment.
